!DCNTL!ORBITAL!ORB.doc: select an orbital (fragment) to be added to the current orbital An elementary unit of a general orbital is a contribution from a single site in a specific unit cell. This contribution can be specified by an angular momentum character or as hybrid orbital. The orbital can be chosen as one of basic types TYPE in a local coordinate system. An existing orbital can be selected using NAME. The orbital needs to be defined by a preceeding !DCNTL!ORBITAL block. In this manner orbitals with arbitrary complexity can be composed. Once defined, the orbital can be shifted by a lattice translation IT and multiplied with a complex factor FAC. The orbital primitives are described further in section sec:dostoolorbitalprimitives.

NAME.rules: optional; incompatible with atom and type
NAME.doc: specifies an orbital previously specified by another block !DCNTL!ORBITAL!ORB

FAC.doc: Orbital coefficient, with which it contributes to the orbital to be built.

IT.doc: translations along the three real space lattice vectors. The entire orbital is shifted by $\sum_{j=1}^3\vec{T}_j IT_j$.

ATOM.doc: atom name on which the orbital resides. (Extended notation, see section sec:extendedatomnotation on p. sec:extendedatomnotation)

TYPE.rules: optional; incompatible with name; mandatory if atom is specified.
TYPE.doc: orbital type. Can be one of the following: 'S', 'PX', 'PY', 'PZ', 'SP1', 'SP2', 'SP3', 'DXY', 'DZ2' or 'D3Z2-R2', 'DXZ', 'DYZ', 'DX2-Y2', 'FX(X2-3Y2)', 'FZ(X2-Y2)', 'FXZ2' or 'FZ(5Z2-R2)', 'FZ3' or 'FZ(5Z2-3R2)' 'FXZ2' or 'FY(5Z2-R2)', 'FXYZ', 'FY(3X2-Y2)' The meaning of these keywords is described in section sec:dostoolorbitalprimitivesangularmomentum Only the first orbital per angular momentum is used. This omission can be undesired, in particular, when core states are treated like valence states.

Z.doc: vector defining the new z-direction to which TYPE refers

NNZ.doc: atom name of the atom to which the vector defining the new z-direction points. (Extended notation, see section sec:extendedatomnotation on p. sec:extendedatomnotation)

X.doc: vector defining the new xz-plane together with z to which TYPE refers

NNX.doc: atom name of the atom to which the vector defining the new x-direction points. (Extended notation, see section sec:extendedatomnotation on p. sec:extendedatomnotation)

!DCNTL!WEIGHT.doc: defines orbital weights; three ways to specify the weights are possible specify "TYPE"; rather unspecific selections such as total density of states. specify one or several sub-blocks "!ATOM"; selects contributions from different atoms. specify one or several sub-blocks "!ORB". Most specific version, identifying individual orbitals The selection type is not compatible with the other two possibilities.

ID.doc: defines the name for this set of matrix elements. This ID defines the name of the output file as PREFIX//ID//'.dos', where PREFIX is defined in !DCNTL!GENERIC:PREFIX. The file format is described in section sec:formatdosfile

LEGEND.doc: defines the legend used in the plot to annotate the dataset.

TYPE.rules: optional; if type is specified, no blocks !atom or !orbs must be present
TYPE.doc: specifies how the weights are defined; can be ["ALL"] sum over all projected density of states ["EMPTY"] weight of the wave function not considered in any projection ["TOTAL"] total density of states

SPIN.doc: specifies the axis $\vec{e}_S$ for the spin projection. The density of states is divided into contributions from eigenstates into spin eigenstates parallel and anti-parallel to this spin axis. (Even non-spin polarized calculations are interpreted in the data model for non-collinear calculations.) The parallel contribution is shown with positive values and the antiparallel contribution is shown with negative values. ['TOTAL'] Both spin components are added up. (The second component is set to zero.) ['X' or '+X'] spin axis is $\vec{e}_S=(1,0,0)$ ['-X'] spin axis is $\vec{e}_S=(-1,0,0)$ ['Y' or '+Y'] spin axis is $\vec{e}_S=(0,1,0)$ ['-Y'] spin axis is $\vec{e}_S=(0,-1,0)$ ['Z' or '+Z'] spin axis is $\vec{e}_S=(0,0,1)$ ['-Z'] spin axis is $\vec{e}_S=(0,0,-1)$ ['MAIN'] spin axis is the direction of the majority spin axis. [string holding three real numbers] The three numbers are the three cartesian components of the spin axis $\vec{e}_S$

!DCNTL!WEIGHT!ATOM.doc: select the angular momentum weights from a given atom.

NAME.doc: atom name from which the contribution to this weight is selected

TYPE.doc: selects the weights from this atom. Can be ["ALL"] sum over all projected density of states on this atom ["S"] angular-momentum weight for $\ell=0$ ["P"] angular-momentum weight for $\ell=1$ ["D"] angular-momentum weight for $\ell=2$ ["F"] angular-momentum weight for $\ell=3$ or a combination of S,P,D,F, such as "SD".

!DCNTL!COOP.doc: selects off-diagonal matrix elements of the density-of-states operator. The off-diagonal elements are defined by all pairs of orbitals specified in !DCNTL!COOP!ORB1 on the one hand and in !DCNTL!COOP!ORB2 on the other hand. While it is possible, it is not recommended to use more than one pair of orbitals. The result of multiple orbitals is the sum of all coops that can be built from orbitals all pairs of orbitals, of which one is from ORB1 and the other from ORB2. The result is identical to the matrix element of an orbital obtained by summing all orbitals ORB1 and another one obtained by summing all orbitals ORB2.

ID.doc: defines the name for this set of matrix elements. This ID defines the name of the output file as PREFIX//ID//'.dos', where PREFIX is defined in !DCNTL!GENERIC:PREFIX. The file format is described in section sec:formatdosfile

LEGEND.doc: defines the legend used in the plot to annotate the dataset.

SPIN.doc: specifies the axis $\vec{e}_S$ for the spin projection. The density of states is projected onto contributions from spin eigenstates parallel (not antiparallel) to this spin axis. (Even non-spin polarized calculations are interpreted in the data model for non-collinear calculations.) ['TOTAL'] Both spin components are added up. (The second component is set to zero.) ['X' or '+X'] spin axis is $\vec{e}_S=(1,0,0)$ ['-X'] spin axis is $\vec{e}_S=(-1,0,0)$ ['Y' or '+Y'] spin axis is $\vec{e}_S=(0,1,0)$ ['-Y'] spin axis is $\vec{e}_S=(0,-1,0)$ ['Z' or '+Z'] spin axis is $\vec{e}_S=(0,0,1)$ ['-Z'] spin axis is $\vec{e}_S=(0,0,-1)$ ['MAIN'] spin axis is the direction of the majority spin axis. [string holding three real numbers] The three numbers are the three cartesian components of the spin axis $\vec{e}_S$

!DCNTL!COOP!ORB1.doc: selects the 'left' orbital of the density of states matrix element Usage is same as !DCNTL!ORBITAL!ORB

!DCNTL!COOP!ORB2.doc: selects the 'right' orbital of the density of states matrix element Usage is same as !DCNTL!ORBITAL!ORB

!DPCNTL.doc: containes directions on what the tool shall do

EZERO[EV].doc: shifts the energy axis of all graphs so the specified value (in eV) is the new energy zero. (Often this is chosen as the highest occupied state, respectively the Fermi level.) may be overwritten by EZERO in !graph and !set

EMIN[EV].doc: lower bound (in eV) of the energy interval shown

EMAX[EV].doc: upper bound (in eV) of the energy interval shown

YMIN.doc: lower bound in 1/eV of the density-of-states interval shown. A negative value allows to also show the opposite spin direction.

YMAX.doc: upper bound in 1/eV of the density-of-states interval shown.

PREFIX.doc: Default for the prefix used in this graph. The name of the density of states data produced by paw_dos are constructed by appending the prefix specified here to the set-id, and by appending the extension '.dos'.

SCALE.doc: default value for the scale factor of the Density of States used in this graph

EZERO[EV].doc: shifts the energy axis of sets in this graph so the specified value (in eV) is the new energy zero. May be overwritten by EZERO in !SET.

YMIN.doc: lower bound in 1/eV of the density-of-states interval shown. A negative value allows to also show the opposite spin direction.

YMAX.doc: upper bound in 1/eV of the density-of-states interval shown.

!DPCNTL!GRAPH!SET.doc: Defines a set of density of states. A set contains the density of states (irrespective of their occupation) density of states weighted with occupation For collinear spin polarized calculation, the spin-up density is written first followed by the spin down density.

ID.doc: identifier for set. The name of the density of states data produced by paw_dos are constructed by appending the prefix to the set-id, and by appending the extension '.dos'.

PREFIX.doc: Prefix used for this set. The name of the density of states data produced by paw_dos are constructed by appending the prefix specified here to the set-id, and by appending the extension '.dos'.

SCALE.doc: scale factor of the Density of States used in this graph

EZERO[EV].doc: shifts the energy axis for this set so the specified value (in eV) is the new energy zero.

STACK.doc: If true, this set is added ontop of an existing stack. This redefines the new set and the stack. If STACK is non-existent or has the value .false. the stack is reset to the actual set.

COLOR.doc: Fills the density of states with color. The colors to the left of the following table may be used. The corresponding colors on the right will be used for the empty density of states. black {RGB}{0 , 0, 0} grey {RGB}{200,200,200} red {RGB}{255, 0, 0} green {RGB}{ 0,230, 0} blue {RGB}{ 0, 0,255} yellow {RGB}{230,230, 0} cyan {RGB}{ 0,230,230} magenta {RGB}{255, 0,255} orange {RGB}{255,165, 0} brown {RGB}{200,150,150} gold {RGB}{170,130, 0} darkgreen {RGB}{ 0,155, 0} lblack {RGB}{150,150,150} lgrey {RGB}{240,240,240} lred {RGB}{255,150,150} lgreen {RGB}{170,255,170} lblue {RGB}{150,150,255} lyellow {RGB}{255,255,150} lcyan {RGB}{150,255,255} lmagenta {RGB}{255,150,255} lorange {RGB}{255,210,120} lbrown {RGB}{255,180,180} lgold {RGB}{210,180,100} ldarkgreen{RGB}{120,220,120} name RGB name RGB black black {white{(000,000,000)}} lblack lblack {(150,150,150)} grey grey {(200,200,200)} lgrey lgrey {(240,240,240)} red red {(255,000,000)} lred lred {(255,150,150)} green green {(000,230,000)} lgreen lgreen {(150,255,150)} blue blue {white{(000,000,255)}} lblue lblue {(150,150,255)} yellow yellow {(230,230,000)} lyellow lyellow {(255,255,150)} cyan cyan {(000,230,230)} lcyan lcyan {(150,255,255)} magenta magenta {(255,000,255)} lmagenta lmagenta {(255,150,255)} orange orange {(255,165,000)} lorange lorange {(255,210,120)} brown brown {(200,150,150)} lbrown lbrown {(255,180,180)} gold gold {(170,130,000)} lgold lgold {(210,180,100)} darkgreen darkgreen {(000,155,000)} ldarkgreen ldarkgreen{(120,220,120)}

LEGEND.doc: Switch to include a legend-block in the plot when true.

!BCNTL.doc: Control file for band structure calculations

NAME.default: Rootname of the project with extension '.banddata'
NAME.doc: File name of banddata file from paw calculation. Usually the extension of the file name is '.banddata' and the main part is equal to the rootname of the calculation.

!BCNTL!BANDSTRUCTURE.doc: defines the bandstructure to be computed and plotted including fatbands

MODE.doc: Mode of the calculation of the bandstructure. The two possible values are 'LINEARINTERPOLATION" and 'DIAG', which are described below. The value 'DIAG' may be replaced by 'DIAGONALISATION' or 'DIAGONALIZATION'.
MODE.note: manual vdescr has a doubled quote after 'LINEARINTERPOLATION'; allowed list transcribed by hand

METHOD_DIAG.doc: Method used for the diagonalisation of the paw Hamiltonian (generalized eigenvalue problem). Currently the two Lapack-functions zhegvd (method_diag=1) and zhegv (method_diag=2) can be used.

EPWPSI.doc: Planewave cutoff in Rydberg for the calculation of the eigenstates of the paw hamiltonian. The default is to use the same value as in the paw calculation, which is stored in the banddata-file. Details are described below.

!BCNTL!BANDSTRUCTURE!LINE.doc: Line segment in k-space, i.e. a part of a bandstructure

XK1.doc: First point of the line segment in relative coordinates of the reciprocal lattice vectors. The k-point in cartesian coordinates is $\vec{k}$. It is obtained from the relative coordinates $\vec{x}$ by multiplication with the reciprocal lattice vectors $\vec{g}_1$, $\vec{g}_2$, and $\vec{g}_3$as k=g_1 x_1+g_2 x_2+g_3 x_3;.

KVEC1.doc: First point of the line segment in cartesian coordinates.

XK2.doc: Last point of the line segment in relative coordinates of the reciprocal lattice vectors. See the description of variable $xk1$ for the relation of absolute and relative coordinates.

KVEC2.doc: Last point of the line segment in cartesian coordinates.

KVECSCALE.doc: scale factor for kvec1 and kvec2 so that they can be given in common coordinates, i.e. $\vec k=\frac{2\pi}{kvecscale}\vec k_{input}$.

SPIN.doc: spin direction. In a spin-polarized collinear calculation the parameter can have the values 1 or 2.

NK.doc: number of grid points along the line segment.

NKDIAG.doc: number of grid points along the line segment for diagonalisation. IF NKDIAG$<$NK the bands obtained from the diagonalisation of the paw hamiltonian will be interpolated using a 1D-FFT. NKDIAG$>$NK causes an error.

XKPROJECT.doc: direction for the projection for 2-d band structures in relative coordinates of the reciprocal lattice vectors. Not yet implemented for METHOD=1.

NPROJECT.rules: optional, must be an odd number
NPROJECT.doc: number of displaced band line segments for the projection for 2-d band structures. Not yet implemented for METHOD=1.

TAPPEND.doc: If TAPPEND is true, then the output data from the current line segment will be appended at the end of the file FILE. The default behaviour, i.e. when TAPPEND is false or not given, an existing file FILE will be overwritten.

!BCNTL!BANDSTRUCTURE!LINE!FATBAND.doc: defines an orbital projected band structure (fat bands). This rudimentary interface will be extended in the future. Currently only projections $|\langle\tilde p_{IPRO} |\tilde \psi_i\rangle|^2$ are used, which are not comparable in magnitude between different IPRO, i.e. fatbands of different projectors should not be compared with respect to their relative magnitude.

IPRO.doc: number of projector for the calculation of the projected band structure.

LINESPERBAND.doc: number of lines per band to draw in band structure in order to represent the value of the projection.

MAXWIDTH.doc: maximal width in eV of bands in projected band structure.

FILE.default: data are appended to previously specified file.

!BCNTL!PDOS.doc: defines the calculation of energy eigenvalues and projections, i.e. the calculation of a new PDOS-file, which is compatible with the one produced from the main paw program.

NKDIV.doc: fractions of reciprocal lattice vectors defining the reciprocal sublattice for the k-points. See also !STRUCTURE!KPOINTS!DIV
NKDIV.note: manual gives no \vdefault for this mandatory key (lines 8174-8179)

PDOSINFILE.doc: filename of the PDOS-file to be read.

PDOSOUTFILE.doc: filename of the new PDOS-file to be written.

NB.doc: number of bands. This parameter does not influence the computational complexity, because the full spectrum of the paw hamiltonian is calculated. It only determines the number of bands in the output files.

SPACEGROUP.doc: Symmetry of the crystal used for reducing the number of k-points that have to be calculated. Sequential number according to International Tables for Crystallography, Vol. A. See description below.

TSHIFT.doc: setting TSHIFT to true excludes the Gamma point from the set of k-points.

ISHIFT.doc: defines a shift of the k-point grid.

!PCNTL.doc: defines the operations done on the system; largely independent of the system

!PCNTL!GENERIC.doc: defines optimization parameters (and use of the trace)

TRACE.doc: writes information on the calls of subroutines to standard output

TOL.doc: tolerance of the maximal component of the force on atoms in the convergence cycles

NSTEPS.doc: maximal number of steps for the convergence. After that number the structure optimization is stopped no matter if the forces have become smaller than TOL. A statement on the convergence will be written to the protocol.

!PCNTL!FILES.doc: specifies the file names that deviate from the standard values

ID.doc: identifier for the file; options are: ['PROT']protocol file Standard extension:'.pprot' ['STRC'] The structure file as used by the simulation code. Used for the input structure. Standard extension:'.strc' ['XYZ'] data file with the resulting optimized structure Standard extension:'.xyz'

NAME.doc: filename. Can be the relative file name or an extension to the PAW "root". Standard output can be specified by NAME='stdout' and EXT=.false.

EXT.doc: T: NAME specifies the extension only. F: full name

!PCNTL!OUTPUT.doc: specifies which information should be written to the protocol

PRINTATOMS.doc: information on the used atom parameterization and freezing is written to the protocol

PRINTBONDS.doc: information on the used bonds is written to the protocol

WARNFF.doc: paw_preopt tries to find best-suiting force fields for the atoms. However, in some cases it cannot decide which parameterization will be the best. If T in these cases a warning will be printed to the protocol.

XYZOUT.doc: should an xyz-file of the resulting structure be created?

!PCNTL!FREEZEONLY.rules: optional, not used if !PCNTL!MOVEONLY is present
!PCNTL!FREEZEONLY.doc: sets freezing of all atoms but those specified in this block to false. May be overwritten for single atoms by !STRC!ATOM:FREEZE

PART.doc: Specifies a part of an atom name. All atoms containing this string are used. Case is ignored.

!PCNTL!MOVEONLY.doc: sets freezing of all atoms but those specified in this block to true. May be overwritten for single atoms by !STRC!ATOM:FREEZE

PART.doc: Specifies a part of an atom name. All atoms containing this string are used. Case is ignored.

!STRC!ATOM.doc: usage is same as in the main simulation code. Keywords R, SP and NAME are used. Additional keywords are:

FFTYPE.default: depending on the atom type and the number of bonds to that atom
FFTYPE.doc: Force field type used for this atom. This keyword can be used to overwrite the suggestion of the program. Possible force fields can be found in section sec:UFF on page sec:UFF.

!STRC!BOND.doc: Overwrite the suggestion of the program for bonds between the atoms. Not yet implemented.
